These can trigger geomagnetic storms and other space weather effects.

The flare that erupted on July 15, 2002 was the most energetic of the year. It was visible from the ground in all but the darkest areas of the Northern Hemisphere. The flare featured a huge coronal mass ejection (CME), which is a cloud of solar material and magnetic fields that can travel at up to 830,000 miles per hour.

The solar wind, the stream of high-energy particles that streams out of the Sun, can cause problems for Earth's magnetosphere, the region of space around our planet that shields us from radiation from the Sun. But S&P also warned that the U.S. could still avoid such a downgrade, which would put it in the same league as companies that sell junk bonds. That would make U.S. bonds a poor investment for pension funds and other investors.

—The rating agency is waiting for the next debt ceiling showdown to make a final call. The U.S. Treasury is expected to exhaust its borrowing capacity by mid-October unless Congress raises it.

French people often say “Non” to questions that they think are an attempt to make a nuisance of themselves, and will not respond directly if a question is asked that is not quite a question.

"It's not a good idea to put them in bed with you," she said. "They don't have the ability to regulate their body temperature. If you are going to stay in bed all day, it's not a good idea to have them in there."

If you do decide to put your dog or cat in bed with you, make sure they have a warm bed to sleep on and clean bedding.

"You want to make sure that bed has a heating pad underneath it and that it's heated," Johnson said. "We would not recommend that it be on a floor, that's not a good idea for your animal."

She says the best thing you can do is make sure your animal has their own bed - and keep their bedding clean.

"I would recommend the same things I always do, which is keep their bedding clean, their nails short, baths regularly and make sure they know where their food bowl is," she said.

This is not a story about the Church in its early years, but about a single person, Saint Hippolytus, who lived in an age when Christianity was just beginning to flourish. He was born around 215 in Rome, and was a Roman citizen by birth, but was raised a pagan. In his youth, he became involved in a pagan cult and, at least according to one source, was sentenced to be burned alive. Our saint was thus given the name “Hippolytus” (from the Greek “Ho” and “Pylos” meaning “the burnt one”). Hippolytus was canonized by the Catholic Church on June 12, 1779. He is remembered for his piety and love of the Blessed Virgin Mary, and is especially beloved for his devotion to the Blessed Sacrament. He is the patron saint of doctors, athletes, students, and children.

Hogan On Hogan traces the path Hogan took from a young man in small-town America to one of the biggest icons in sporting history. The Securities and Exchange Commission voted 4-to-1 to expand the disclosure requirements for
sampled:
corporate boards of publicly traded companies.
The SEC said it would require the disclosure of three types of information.
One would require companies to tell investors how much of their total pay is tied to short-term performance goals. The SEC also said it would require more detailed disclosure of severance payments to executives who are let go. And it would require companies to inform investors when their corporate officers receive a bonus that exceeds a certain threshold.
The vote came after a public outcry over the pay packages of chief executives and directors. Those payouts have ballooned in recent years, even as the broader economy recovered from the Great Recession.
The SEC's latest proposal "will further increase transparency and empower investors," SEC Chairman Mary Jo White said in a statement. "This move is an important step to help address the increasing concern by investors about CEO pay and the incentive structure of publicly traded companies."
Most business groups support disclosure of the three categories of pay, although they have been divided on whether to require companies to provide more detail about executive severance packages.
The Business Roundtable, which represents the CEOs of America's biggest companies, said in a statement that the SEC "has made a significant and much-needed contribution to the accountability and integrity of the U.S. corporate governance framework."

“Our model attempts to capture people’s moral intuitions that they should maximize their own well-being,” said UCI graduate student and study lead author Thomas Insel, in a statement. “It shows that in the long run, people tend to think it is okay to trade years of life for decades of healthy life.”

Insel and his colleagues created this model based on a paper they wrote in 2012, which showed that people were more likely to choose a longer life if they could do so only after paying a higher price up front. The researchers discovered that the model accurately predicted how people would respond to different life-extending treatments. sampled:

The companies had been engaged in a legal dispute since last November, when Broadcom announced its plans to acquire Qualcomm.
The news of the judge's ruling came after Qualcomm's board of directors had rejected a $105 billion takeover offer from Broadcom, which instead went ahead and bought CA Technologies in a deal worth $19 billion.
Qualcomm disputed Broadcom's acquisition of CA Technologies by arguing that the deal could potentially harm its interests.
In January, Qualcomm asked the court to stop Broadcom from using certain Qualcomm patents in order to make sure that it did not violate a previous court order.
In February, the U.S. International Trade Commission voted to allow the sale of Broadcom's products with chipsets containing a Qualcomm technology.
Qualcomm had filed a lawsuit in January claiming Broadcom had violated the court's order, and that Broadcom was aware of the alleged violations.
In the ruling on Thursday, Judge William Alsup of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California found that Qualcomm had violated the ban on the use of the Patents.
According to the judge, Qualcomm's action "was particularly egregious because it not only directly violated the stay, but also caused harm to Qualcomm's licensing business by weakening the negotiating position of Qualcomm and its customers," the court said in a statement.

The Trojans have a season remaining in which to play for the Pac-12 title and in a bowl. They will not be able to play in a bowl in any circumstances unless the NCAA approves of a sanction reduction.
"We'll be hitting the road recruiting more than we've been hitting the road recruiting, that's for sure," USC offensive coordinator Tee Martin told the Times.
